key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware alloy and device representations to improve predictions for perovskite solar cells with unfamiliar materials and architectures.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber alloys and transport-layer combinations beyond those represented in historical device data.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs from 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with 15.7–19.0% error reductions on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Endpoint interpolation assumes solid-solution continuity; reliability for compositions with phase changes or outside the endpoint coverage remains unclear.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
